summary: I tested v66 Partner Phase 2: partner self-registration, the partner_registration fee, waive/approve, the Stripe payment request and apply_partner_payment. Backend and UI. New suite tests/test_v66_partner_fee.py: 15 of 16 tests pass. The one failure is a known minor security issue: the X-Forwarded-For header can be spoofed to get around the self-register rate limit. The updated test_v65_agents.py passes 22 of 22. The sealed and opening suites (v64, v64b, v64c) pass 66 of 66 with -n 0. I found and fixed one CRITICAL UI bug, the same class of bug as in iteration 137: the new routes /partner/register, /partner/join/:token, /partner/login and /partner/me were nested inside <RequireAdmin> in App.js. I moved them outside. After the fix the whole UI flow works. Sign-in page: five role radios, including signin-role-partner. With Partner selected, the 'Apply to become a PMC partner' link goes to /partner/register. That form shows 'Check your email'. The footer-become-partner link also goes to /partner/register. Old /agent/login still works, and an invalid join token shows agent-join-invalid. In the admin console, the 'Partners' nav item goes to /admin/e/partners. Ticking the waive box shows 'Approve (fee waived)'; unticking it shows 'Send payment request'. Sending the request moved the TEST partner to PAYMENT PENDING and showed 'Registration fee USD 75.00 · pending' and a Resend payment link button. A partner signing in on /login goes to /partner/me. The pay card shows USD 75.00, and the Pay now link points to a checkout.stripe.com cs_test session. After simulating payment with apply_partner_payment, the partner portal shows Approved with code PT-0004, and admin shows the partner code and 'paid on'. The receipt PDF renders (about 50 KB).

minor.issue: The per-IP limit (5 per hour) uses the leftmost X-Forwarded-For value, which the client controls. Sending any X-Forwarded-For header gets around the 429 (I confirmed it returns 200 after the limit was hit). The agent login lockout has the same pattern. Use the rightmost or ingress-appended IP instead.

Once a partner is payment_pending, the admin cannot waive and approve, because approve only accepts the 'submitted' status. The only options left are reject or resend. If that is intended, document it; otherwise allow approve with waive_fee from payment_pending.
This endpoint has no CSRF dependency, unlike the other agent POST endpoints. Low risk because it only reads Stripe status, but it is inconsistent.
PDF and attachment errors are swallowed with a bare 'except Exception: pass' and nothing is logged, so a missing receipt would go unnoticed. Add logger.exception.

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED by testing agent: the /partner/register, /partner/join/:token, /partner/login and /partner/me routes were inside <RequireAdmin>, so every unauthenticated partner was bounced to the admin login.

integration_issues.issue: When the email fails, the toast 'Payment request created — email did not send' is shown in success (green) style. It should use toast.warning or toast.error.
If the payment is still unpaid, the button gives no feedback (no toast), so the user can't tell anything happened.

issues: The banking line shows stray separators ('· TEST · 123456789 ·') when the institution name or currency is empty.
The note placeholder still says 'Note to the agent'. Rename it to 'partner'.
The 'Check your email' card has no link back to the home page or to sign in.

action_items: Keep the /partner/* routes outside RequireAdmin in App.js (already fixed). Avoid adding public routes inside the RequireAdmin block in future.
Use a trusted client IP (rightmost or ingress-appended X-Forwarded-For) for the self-register and login rate limits.
Decide whether waive and approve should be allowed from payment_pending.
Show the 'email did not send' toast as a warning; give feedback when 'check again' finds the payment still unpaid.
Log exceptions in apply_partner_payment receipt generation.
critical_code_review_comments: Public routes were added inside RequireAdmin again (the same regression as iteration 137). Consider grouping all public partner and agent routes in one block with a comment.

The partner_code sequence is never reset. TEST runs used PT-0001 to PT-0004. I deleted the counters doc {name: partner_code} because no agents remain, and test cleanup now resets it when the agents collection is empty.
There are no country-group fee rules beyond the 'countries' list. A KE+TZ group rule matched KE correctly.
seed_data_creation: All TEST data was cleaned up: agents test_partner_*, emd_masters 'TEST*' partner_registration rules, payment_transactions for TEST agents, reg: rate-limit attempts, and the partner_code counter. The agents collection is now empty.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run pytest tests/test_v66_partner_fee.py tests/test_v65_agents.py -n 0. The xff spoof test fails by design until the IP fix lands. For UI: run `python tests/ui_partner_setup.py` to create a submitted KE partner (test_partner_ui_v66@example.com / PartnerPw@123) plus a USD 75 KE rule, and `python tests/ui_partner_setup.py cleanup` to remove them. Simulate payment with routers.agents.apply_partner_payment(session_id) (see the _apply helper in test_v66). Admin Playwright login: page.request.post to /api/v1/admin/auth/login, then sessionStorage pmc.csrf. Sending email to example.com always fails (email_sent false).
